FIND: The `section_terminator` regex in `parse_admissibility_block` (lines 82–86) uses only `re.MULTILINE` and is therefore case‑sensitive. The `marker_match` for the ADMISSIBILITY header uses `re.IGNORECASE`, so the block start is detected regardless of case. If a model writes the next section header in mixed or lower case (e.g. `"novelty:"`, `"Verified:"`), the terminator fails to match, causing the ADMISSIBILITY block to overrun into subsequent sections. That can pull text from later sections into the gate search, causing false PASS/FAIL results. This is a regression in this slice – the issue was previously fixed in the baseline (see closed C0022) but is not reflected here.
FOLLOW: The `failed` list returned by the function is used by the feedback channel to instruct models which gates to supply or fix. An incorrectly scoped block can mis‑classify gates, undermining the correction loop. Downstream consumers of the admissibility status would receive wrong information.
ANALYSE: HARD (correctness). The parser must reliably isolate the ADMISSIBILITY block; otherwise its output is wrong. CONFIRMED – the code clearly omits `re.IGNORECASE`.
FIX: Add `re.IGNORECASE` to the `section_terminator` regex.

CONFIRM C0026 | The parser stops at the first match for a gate (break after match), ignoring later occurrences. If a model writes contradictory statuses for the same gate (e.g. `d_tool: PASS … d_tool: FAIL`), the parser will report PASS. This is a genuine bug that can produce false passes. The finding is correct. I propose an extension: instead of breaking on first match, collect all statuses for the gate and consider it FAILED if any status is FAIL.

CHALLENGE C0033 | The function returning all gates when `finding_text` is empty is correct behaviour: no text implies no ADMISSIBILITY block, therefore all gates are failed. This is intentional design and does not constitute a bug. The finding is based on a misunderstanding.

CHALLENGE C0039 | The current code does not define or use a `gate_line_pattern`; gate matching is performed with `re.search()` over the entire block without line anchoring. Therefore a numbered‑list prefix (e.g. `1. S_min: PASS`) does not prevent the regex from matching. The finding is stale for this version of the code and should be withdrawn.
